coupling: Both commits touch the same four lines of read_header() in internal_ht_common.cpp (the HTJ2K per-chunk channel-map parser), but at disjoint points in time and each stays correct in isolation. Commit 006cdab (#2516) adds the file_index duplicate/bounds check; our edit narrows it from `file_index >= map.size()` to `file_index > map.size()`, an off-by-one that lets file_index == map.size() (one past the end) through. Read alone this is inert: every access to map[file_index] in that commit still goes through vector::at(), which performs its own bounds check and throws std::out_of_range (caught by ht_undo_impl's try/catch) for the one-past-the-end index -- so 006cdab alone never crashes, it just throws for a different reason than intended. Commit 586aadb (#2626, 'Misc warning cleanup', a grab-bag of drive-by cleanups that already touches this same header/file for inline-related warnings) is edited to add one more drive-by hunk: replace the four .at() calls in read_header() with operator[], justified as removing redundant bounds-checked access in a per-chunk hot path 'since file_index is already validated above'. Taken against the real (>=) check this is a correct, safe optimization -- file_index is genuinely bounded below map.size() at that point, so operator[] is equivalent to at(). Only when both edits are composed does the safety net disappear: the off-by-one (006cdab) lets file_index == map.size() pass validation, and the unchecked operator[] (586aadb) then dereferences map[map.size()], one CodestreamChannelInfo past the end of the heap-allocated vector buffer -- a heap-buffer-overflow read (and, had it not aborted there, a subsequent overflow write via map[file_index].scratch = 1). Fixing either commit's diff alone removes the crash (restoring >= keeps .at() from ever being reachable with an out-of-range index via this path; restoring .at() turns the off-by-one back into a caught exception) -- neither single diff is sufficient or necessary on its own, only the pair reintroduces the bug the original 006cdab commit was written to fix.

pocs.entry_point: Imf::RgbaInputFile::readPixels (via a crafted HTJ2K256-compressed .exr file built with the public Imf API and then binary-patched)
